citation: Gore, J. M., Miller, A., Fray, L., Harris, J., & Prieto, E. (2021). Improving student achievement through professional development: Results from a randomised controlled trial of Quality Teaching Rounds. Teaching and Teacher Education, 101, 103297. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tate.2021.103297
url: https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/54403979 (published OA version, CC-BY-NC-ND, deposited in University of Newcastle openresearch repository; landing http://hdl.handle.net/1959.13/1426058 -> https://openresearch.newcastle.edu.au/articles/.../29012696)
design: Four-arm cluster RCT (assignment = School), NSW government primary schools, Australia. 133/134 schools analysed, 125 PLCs, 234 classes, n=5478 Stage 2 students (Years 3-4, ages 8-10), Cohort 1 only (Cohort 2 postponed to 2021 due to COVID). Arms: (1) Researcher-led QTR [QTR], (2) Trainer-led QTR [QTR-T], (3) Peer Observation (active alternative-PD control), (4) Wait-list Control (business-as-usual reference). Pedagogy-focused TPD (Quality Teaching Rounds), Short duration. Primary outcomes = student achievement in mathematics, reading and science via ACER Progressive Achievement Tests (PAT), baseline and 8-month follow-up. ITT linear mixed models (random intercepts for school and class) with covariates; impacts as group-by-time contrasts vs the wait-list control. Grades 3-4 (K-2/3-5 band -> 3-5).
problems: The meta-analysis lists exactly TWO arms (row_ids 38 and 39) for this four-arm trial. The contrast required by the spec is TPD vs BUSINESS-AS-USUAL (no alternative treatment). Two arms qualify: Researcher-led QTR (QTR) and Trainer-led QTR (QTR-T), both compared against the wait-list Control. The Peer Observation arm is an ACTIVE ALTERNATIVE-PD control (its own PD programme, time/funding matched), not business-as-usual, so it is NOT extracted (and that exclusion is what leaves exactly two qualifying arms, consistent with the meta-analysis). Arm->row assignment is by my convention: row_id 38 = QTR (researcher-led; the headline arm), row_id 39 = QTR-T (trainer-led). The meta-analysis cannot tell us which numbered row maps to which arm; if central records reverse this, the two arms are symmetric in coding (both 'Comprehensive approaches', School, RCT, Short, Mixed, Res/Dev). g values reported here are taken DIRECTLY from Table 6 column 'Adjusted effect size g (95% CI)' (and confirmed in text), so they are already Hedges' g: the paper computed g via R's compute.es (Hedges & Olkin 1985) on the model-based change-score contrast (intervention change minus control change), standardised by the UNCONDITIONAL pooled change-score SD s* = sqrt(((n1-1)s1^2+(n2-1)s2^2)/(n1+n2-2)). No further J correction applied by me. g_se and g_var are derived from each reported 95% CI: g_se = (hi-lo)/(2*1.959964), g_var = g_se^2; these CIs are narrower than the naive single-level Hedges-Olkin var formula would give because compute.es derived variance from the model-based estimate. impact_se not separately printed. mean_t/sd_t/mean_c/sd_c are the 8-month posttest mean and (unconditional) SD from Appendix A; impact_estimate recorded is the adjusted mean difference (intervention change minus control change) from Table 6, NOT the standardised g (g is in the g field). cluster_adjusted=true (multilevel ITT model accounts for school+class clustering). icc=null: no observed/empirical ICC for these outcomes is reported; the paper only assumed a conservative ICC=0.38 at the power-calculation (design) stage (noted per effect), which the spec says not to use as the design-effect ICC. n_clusters recorded as the number of SCHOOLS in the relevant intervention arm (QTR=37, QTR-T=34) plus control (31); the value stored is the intervention-arm school count. n_t/n_c are the Table 6 baseline analysis n per arm (model n); valid-follow-up retained n (n minus n-miss) is given in notes. Science PAT had only one test level per grade and the authors flag possible ceiling/floor effects (students answering all items correctly at baseline were removed); science still mapped to STEM per spec. Only the immediate end-of-treatment wave (8-month follow-up, Cohort 1) exists in this report; no later waves.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Researcher-led QTR (QTR): two-day QT/QTR workshop + four in-school PD days; teachers form PLCs running Quality Teaching Rounds. vs wait-list (business-as-usual) Control
effect_sizes.test_name: ACER Progressive Achievement Test - Mathematics (PAT-M v4)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (8-month follow-up; Term 4 2019; end of treatment, Cohort 1)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported directly as Hedges' g in Table 6, 'Adjusted effect size g (95% CI)' = 0.12 (0.07, 0.17). Paper's g = (x2-x1)/s* on the model-based change-score contrast (intervention change minus control change), standardised by unconditional pooled change-score SD; computed via R compute.es (Hedges & Olkin 1985). g_se = (0.17-0.07)/(2*1.959964); g_var = g_se^2. impact_estimate = adjusted mean difference 1.55 (0.87, 2.23) change-score points. mean/SD are 8-month posttest from Appendix A (unconditional).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.9 Table 6 (Mathematics, QTR row); p.10 Appendix A (means/SDs); g also stated p.6 (g=0.12, 95% CI 0.07-0.17)
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory result: QTR made ~25% / two months more maths progress than control; group-by-time p<0.000, post-hoc p=0.000 (significant). Model n=1307; valid follow-up retained n=1165 (142 missing). Equivalent to ~2 months additional growth (EEF). Design-stage power ICC assumption was 0.38 (not an observed outcome ICC; not used).
